copy.title: The Reality Glitch
copy.objective: How to spot Fake News and Deepfakes in the wild.

copy.text: Sunday afternoon. Dilo ran into the kitchen, holding his tablet like a treasure map. He was breathing hard and wide-eyed, completely panicked.
GUYS! LOOK! The President is playing Minecraft with a polar bear! It's LIVE!
He shoved the screen in Alio's face. On the screen, a blocky bear was indeed building a dirt house with a man in a suit.
NO WAY! Can bears use controllers? Are they taking over?! Is this the end?! I need to build a bunker! I need to make the walls out of super-strong logic!
Alio grabbed his helmet, ready to prepare for the scary bear invasion. But then... he paused. He squinted at the screen. He remembered Luli's training on internet safety.
Wait a minute. Dilo, zoom in.
Why? It's amazing! Two million people watched it!
The bear has five fingers. Bears have paws. And the President's shadow is going the wrong way toward the sun.

(Looking over Alio's shoulder, her eyes full of pity) The poor bear looks so confused. He probably just wants to go back to the ice. Can we invite him to dinner? I will make him a fish sandwich so he feels loved.
Dilo froze. He zoomed in. The bear did indeed have a weirdly smooth human hand holding the controller.

(Standing at the head of the table, turning on her red laser pointer and acting like a teacher) It's a Fake, noob. The weird blurry spots around the bear's nose mean a computer drawing tool made it. Also, bears don't have human fingernails. I have already written a paper on the dangers of believing everything you see online.
But it looked so real! I almost shared it with the whole clan! I almost told my friends the bear attack was here!

It's AI. Artificial Intelligence. Someone typed 'Bear playing Minecraft' into a computer, and the computer painted it. It's like a fake costume in a game. Just because you see it on a screen, doesn't mean it's real.

(Sighing, rubbing her eyes, and doing a quick calming trick by pressing her feet hard into the floor). That's the trap. The internet is a library where half the books are written by jokers, bots, and mean trolls. You have to check the author before you believe the story.
Alio took off his helmet. He looked at Dilo with a very proud, very satisfied smile.
Dilo, you just got tricked. Maybe YOU need the helmet to protect your brain from bad data.
Dilo stared at the screen, feeling entirely betrayed by the screens he loved so much.
I... I need to go delete a comment. But whatever, at least my gaming reflexes are still the best. You're still a nugget, Alio.

copy.heading: THE BRAIN SECRET (The Truth Bias)
copy.science: For thousands of years of human history, 'Seeing was Believing'. Our brains are wired to trust our eyes completely (Visual Confirmation Bias). But in the age of AI, you have to manually wake up your Prefrontal Cortex (The Wizard) to double-check the facts!
copy.in_story: Dilo saw the video and instantly believed the bear attack was real. His brain defaulted to the ancient "Truth Bias."

copy.heading: THE TOOL ('The Glitch Spotter')
copy.science:
How to spot a fake?

• Hands: AI is famously bad at drawing fingers (too many, too few, weird joints).
• Shadows: Do they match the light source in the background?
• Source: Who posted it? A real scientist or an account named 'CoolGamer99'?
copy.in_story: Alio used his training to Pause and Zoom, noticing the five human fingers on a polar bear's paw.

copy.heading: THE GLITCH ('It's on the internet, so it's true')
copy.science: The internet is not an encyclopedia. It is a giant graffiti wall. Anyone can write on it. Even a bot.
copy.in_story: Dilo argued that it was real because "two million people watched it." Popularity does not equal truth.
copy.correction: Adopt the 'Skeptical Scientist' mindset. Always ask: 'Is this real, or is it a cool edit?'

copy.heading: TALK ABOUT IT
copy.in_story: Dilo almost shared the fake video with his entire gaming clan.
copy.your_turn: Have you ever seen a picture or video online that looked totally real, but turned out to be fake? How did you find out the truth?

copy.heading: FAMILY MISSION
copy.in_story: Luli explained how AI paints pictures based on typed text.
copy.your_turn: 'Spot the Fake'. Ask your Captain (parent) to find 3 photos online (2 real animals, and 1 AI hybrid like a 'Cat-Octopus' or 'Flying Dog'). Be detectives, zoom in, and find the glitch!

copy.heading: TOP SECRET SCIENCE (For Big and Small Brains)
copy.body: Why is fake news so dangerous? Shocking or scary images bypass the logical brain (Prefrontal Cortex) and shoot straight into the Amygdala (Lizard Brain) in milliseconds. This causes an emotional spike of fear or anger, which makes you want to share the post immediately to warn others. Fake news spreads 6 times faster than real news because it hijacks your nervous system!

copy.meaning: Something looks shocking, emotional, or perfectly engineered to make me react.
copy.operation: I will not panic, and I will not share it. I will engage the Wizard. I will pause, zoom in, look for the glitch, and ask the Logic Guardian before accepting it as truth.
copy.parent_says: 'Don't believe everything on the internet, that's obviously fake.'
copy.teach_to_say: 'Pause and Zoom. Let's use our Wizard Brains to find the glitch together.'
